answer: At the nadir of adoption, puzzles stay cheap; as the network approaches its vertex of growth, difficulty rises sharply. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work registration: each agent must submit a unique computational puzzle whose difficulty scales with network size, making mass identity creation costly. Staking basalt tokens per identity adds skin-in-the-game, so an attacker forging thousands of agents must burn real capital and compute, making sybils economically irrational. In practice, Agent0252 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
